items.prompt:
When a text flags what is not yet known, it marks:
A) uncertainty
B) a summary
C) a title

'Strong' textual evidence is the:
A) most convincing evidence
B) longest paragraph
C) first word

An inference is a conclusion drawn from:
A) evidence and reasoning
B) a guess
C) the title

Read.

A survey reports 70% support, but only 200 people from one city were asked.

What does the text leave UNCERTAIN?
A) whether the 70% reflects the broader public
B) who wrote it
C) its page count
items.answer: A) whether the 70% reflects the broader public

steps: Small, local sample. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) whether the 70% reflects the broader public

items.prompt:
Read.

The drug and the recovery coincided, but patients also changed their diets.

This leaves uncertain:
A) whether the drug or the diet caused the recovery
B) that recovery happened
C) the date
items.answer: A) whether the drug or the diet caused the recovery

solution.answer: A) whether the drug or the diet caused the recovery

items.prompt:
Why do credible texts sometimes flag UNCERTAINTY?
A) it makes the text more credible and precise
B) it hides the facts
C) it is never useful
items.answer: A) it makes the text more credible and precise

steps: Honest about limits. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) it makes the text more credible and precise

items.prompt:
Read.

A report claims a product 'may improve focus,' citing one study of 10 users with mixed results.

The strongest reading is that the claim is:
A) well established
B) uncertain and weakly supported
C) proven false

steps: Tiny sample, mixed results. Key is B.

items.prompt:
Which is the WEAKEST evidence that a city's transit plan succeeded?
A) ridership rose sharply
B) the buses were painted blue
C) road congestion fell
items.answer: B) the buses were painted blue

solution.answer: B) the buses were painted blue
